agents.report:
Barrick (B) is falling today because gold is breaking down on Fed rate-hike expectations and a strong dollar. I found no company-specific news today. Sources agree on direction but not always on exact numbers.

**Why it is down today**
- Gold is at a 14-month low, about $3,742–3,772 per ounce intraday. That is down more than 2% on the day, about 6.5% on the week, and roughly a third below January's record near $5,600 ([ActionForex](https://www.actionforex.com/action-insight/market-overview/661273-gold-hits-one-year-low-ahead-of-fomc-minutes-as-fed-rate-path-takes-center-stage/), [Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/article-gold-drops-to-14-month-low-as-hawkish-fed-rhetoric-boosts-dollar/), [Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/11/18/why-is-gold-price-down-today-gold-futures-slip-to-lowest-since-september-2025/)).
- The macro drivers are:
  - October CPI came in hot (0.4% headline, 0.3% core).
  - CME FedWatch puts a December 8–9 hike at about 96% ([FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/gold-tumbles-to-its-lowest-in-over-a-year-as-fed-rate-hike-bets-build-202611181109)).
  - The dollar index is at a 19-month high, and the 10-year yield is around 5.1%.
  - NY Fed President Williams said rates will likely need to rise again.
- Kitco's technical read: gold broke a double bottom near $3,880, which is now resistance. The next test is $3,800, with little support until about $3,500. Silver also made a 52-week low of $46.93 on Monday ([Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/opinion/2026-11-16/precious-metals-break-new-52-week-lows-us-dollar-reaches-new-19-month-high)).
- ActionForex says yields and the dollar don't fully explain the move, so positioning and forced selling may be amplifying it.
- October retail sales were in line (+0.2%). The Fed minutes from the October 27–28 meeting were due at 1:00 PM CT (1900 GMT), after the screen's 12:15 PM CT price, so they are a live event risk for this session.
- Barrick had already been sliding. It fell 2.6% on Monday, and the Canadian shares were down about 10% over seven days as of the Nov 13 close ([Ad-hoc News](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/unternehmensnachrichten/barrick-backs-2026-targets-as-north-american-ipo-filing-and-quarterly-payout-move-in-parallel/70520827)).
- One StockAnalysis snapshot showed $37.09 on Nov 16, with a 52-week range of $34.03–54.69 and an average analyst target around $49.67 ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/b/)). Its low of $34.03 may be a stale figure.

**Q3 results (Nov 9): operations were fine, but costs are rising**
- Revenue was $5.07B, up 22% from a year earlier. Adjusted EPS was $0.82, against about $0.79 expected.
- Gold output was 816,000 ounces, and copper output was 50,000 tonnes, down 11% from Q2.
- Gold all-in sustaining cost (AISC, the full cost per ounce) was $1,911, up from $1,538 a year earlier. The causes were lower grades, higher royalties and diesel. Copper AISC was $4.52 per pound. Realized gold price was $4,243 per ounce.
- Attributable free cash flow fell 44% to $642M. Consolidated free cash flow of $1.17B missed the roughly $1.29B consensus.
- 2026 guidance is unchanged: 2.90–3.25M ounces of gold and 190–220k tonnes of copper. Gold AISC guidance is $1,760–1,950, so Q3 is near the top. The guidance assumes gold at $4,500 per ounce, well above today's price.
- Net cash was $909M, down from $1,245M in Q2. Barrick bought back $761M of stock in the quarter under a $3B program, and total shareholder returns were $1.04B. The program does not obligate it to keep buying.
- The $0.175 dividend is payable Dec 15 to holders of record on Nov 30, which falls inside the 1–10 session window. That is about 0.5% of the share price.
- Sources: [StockTitan release summary](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/B/barrick-reports-third-quarter-2026-0jiyarujpwqk.html), [Q3 results PDF](https://s25.q4cdn.com/322814910/files/doc_news/2026/11/Barrick-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results.pdf), [Barrick Q3 page](https://www.barrick.com/English/news/news-details/2026/q3-2026-results/default.aspx).

**The story and catalysts**
- **IPO of North American assets:** On Nov 10, Barrick filed an S-1 (the SEC registration form for an IPO) for American Barrick Gold, ticker ABGC. It would hold Carlin, Cortez, Turquoise Ridge and Pueblo Viejo, with Fourmile and others to be contributed. Barrick keeps a majority, and the net proceeds are earmarked to be returned to Barrick shareholders. Terms are still blank, and the company targets completion by year-end, subject to market conditions ([SEC S-1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002162540/000119312526455481/d338869ds1.htm), [Investing.com](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/barrick-files-s1-for-american-barrick-gold-ipo-on-nyse-432SI-4972934)).
  - This is a potential unlock, but a gold-price collapse could force a delay or a lower valuation.
  - Mark Hill is named as the incoming CEO of American Barrick, though one source says "Mark Hill will be CEO" without saying of which entity.
- **Fourmile and Newmont:** On Aug 9, Barrick agreed with Newmont to contribute Fourmile to the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture. Newmont pays a $1.95B cash top-up, and outstanding disputes are resolved. On Nov 9 Barrick flagged that the Fourmile pre-feasibility study may be delayed beyond the 2028 target ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9186475/barrick-mining-b-faces-fourmile-study-delay-amid-ipo-plans-shares-rally)).
- **Mali (Loulo-Gounkoto):** The government dispute was settled for $253M (one low-tier outlet says $430M, unverified). Output rose 16% from Q2 and the ramp-up is ahead of schedule. A strike was averted with a union deal around Sept 21–27, but the labor truce is described as fragile, and a contractor exit in May led to lowered 2026 targets for the complex ([Ecofin](https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-industry/0602-52638-barrick-confirms-gold-production-restart-at-mali-s-loulo-gounkoto-mine-in-2026), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-27/barrick-mining-reaches-deal-with-mali-unions-averting-strikes)).
- **Reko Diq (Pakistan):** Barrick slowed development in April on security concerns and is reviewing it through mid-2027. It warned of significant capital and timeline increases. Third-party estimates run to $9.1B with production delayed to 2030. These are not official Barrick numbers ([Northern Miner](https://www.northernminer.com/news/barrick-delays-reko-diq-project-on-security-concerns/1003889411/)). Barrick cut its 2026 capex guidance to $3.8–4.2B because of lower Reko Diq spending.
- **Kibali (DR Congo):** The mine is 45% Barrick, 45% AngloGold Ashanti and 10% state-owned. Barrick temporarily sent home non-essential staff and contractors after two Ebola deaths in a nearby community (internal memo dated Nov 12). It is investigating whether the cases are linked to its workforce. No Ebola cases have been reported at industrial mines, but the outbreak is large (over 11,000 infected and over 5,000 dead nationally, per Reuters). The article does not address production impact ([Miningmx](https://miningmx.com/2026-11-13-barrick-cuts-kibali-workforce-after-nearby-ebola-deaths/)). This is a headline risk.
- **Copper:** The Lumwana expansion in Zambia is on budget, with first copper at the end of Q1 2028, and should roughly double copper output. Copper costs are at the top of guidance.
- **Analysts:**
  - JPMorgan cut its target to $53 from $55 on Nov 10 and kept Overweight.
  - Freedom Broker moved to Hold with a $46 target. Its downgrade is dated Oct 22, but Freedom Broker is also credited with a raised $47 target on Nov 10, which is a conflict between sources. It also downgraded Newmont and Agnico Eagle at the same time ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/freedom-broker-downgrades-barrick-mining-stock-rating-on-reduced-estimates-93CH-4966111)).
  - I found no new downgrade today.

**What it means for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Bearish case:** Gold is in a momentum breakdown with the dollar and rate-hike pricing still rising. The 50-day average is below the 200-day and falling. The next gold support levels are $3,800 and then $3,500. Barrick's costs are near the top of guidance, and guidance assumes gold at $4,500. Further gold weakness hurts the earnings outlook and the IPO valuation.
- **Bounce case:**
  - The stock is at a 52-week low on a 6.8% down day with 1.7 times normal volume, which looks like capitulation.
  - A hike is about 96% priced in, so a dovish surprise in the minutes or from Fed speakers could squeeze gold up.
  - The company has net cash and an active buyback.
  - Q3 was a beat with unchanged guidance.
  - The IPO is a potential catalyst.
  - The Nov 30 dividend record date is in the window.
- **Event risk:** The Fed minutes, other Fed speakers, and Ebola news from Kibali. The Mali and Reko Diq risks are old. No Barrick earnings are due within the window.
- **Key signal:** Whether gold holds $3,742–3,800 or breaks lower. Barrick's behavior will track that more than anything company-specific.

**Gaps**
- I could not confirm Barrick's exact price or percentage move today from a dated source.
- Several sites (Kitco commentary aside) returned 403 errors: Invezz, GuruFocus, the GlobeNewswire release and EBC. I relied on search summaries for those.
- I found nothing on Barrick after Nov 17, and no CEO-departure news.

- Demand growth in 2026 is put at about 30%, mostly from end use rather than inventory building. They see 2027 demand up 15–20% to about 2.5M tons, and above 3M tons by 2030.
- Capex is unchanged at about $3B over 2026–2028, even at current prices.
- Novandino (the Salar de Atacama operation, run with Codelco) is guided to about 290kt in 2026 and slightly above 300kt in 2027. Management expects costs to stay flat.
- Mt Holland (the Australian spodumene mine) is guided to 175–185kt in 2026.
- The specialty plant nutrition (SPN) volume growth outlook was cut to about 5% from about 10%. Management said Q3 was weak across more than 100 countries and blamed higher phosphate-based product prices.
- 2027 potassium chloride volumes will be lower than in 2026.
- Iodine looks steady.

**The wider lithium picture.**
- China's spot lithium carbonate peaked above 200,000 yuan/t in May. The 209,880 figure is from one report, and Bloomberg's figures put the 2026 drop at about 23% to about 91,500 yuan.
- GFEX futures are down more than 40% from a late-August high. They were volatile this week at roughly 88,000–93,000 yuan.
- Benchmark's Daisy Jennings-Gray cited speculative selling on GFEX, high battery-cell inventories, and expected supply additions as the drivers.
- Possible new supply includes Bald Hill and Finniss restarts, firmer Zimbabwe ore flows, and a possible restart of CATL's Jianxiawo mine.
- Forecasts disagree. Benchmark sees a deficit of 171kt in 2026 and 44kt in 2027, then a surplus from 2028. S&P Global says many Chinese participants expect a 2027 surplus.
- Citi cut its 2-year lithium price forecasts by as much as 40%, citing slower battery demand growth and trade uncertainty. I couldn't open the article, so the date is unknown.
- The LIT lithium-miners ETF hit a 12-month low of $56.42 on Nov 17, down 12% in 20 sessions. Rising US bond yields and a firmer dollar also hit miners on Nov 12.
- Albemarle warned that Q4 sales and profit will fall on lower prices. It is about 56% below its April high.
- Lithium stocks hit six-month lows on Oct 30 in a broader mining sell-off.
- Lithium carbonate bounced about 3–5% on Nov 17–18 in China, so there is a tentative stabilization.

**SQM-specific context.**
- The stock is down about 46% from its April high (one source). The Nov 16 MarketBeat alert had the 50-day average at about $63 and the 200-day at about $74.
- Analyst moves: JPMorgan upgraded to overweight on Nov 6 but cut its target from $88 to $71. Deutsche Bank cut its target from $94 to $81 on Oct 27. Zacks went to strong sell on Oct 23. Consensus targets run about $78–80.
- Many targets are stale and will likely be cut after today's report. I did not find post-earnings analyst actions.
- Balance sheet at Sept 30: cash $2.69B, other current financial assets $2.34B, total debt about $5.5B. Valuation was about 10.8 times earnings on Nov 16.
- A special dividend of $1.435 per share was paid Sept 21.
- Chile risk looks lower. The Codelco joint venture (Nova Andino Litio) secures Atacama operations to 2060. Kast has said he will respect the contracts, though a review of national lithium strategy is planned. Sources describing it are commentary, not a government document.
- Tianqi, which holds about 22% of SQM, approved a sale of 1.25% of its holding in February. It had first filed to sell 100%, then withdrew that notice minutes later. It could weigh on the stock as an overhang.

**For a 1–10 session trade.**
- The move is a post-earnings gap down to new lows. It combines a modest miss, a guidance warning about Q4 pricing, and a sector already in a heavy downtrend.
- The bear case is that Q4 realized price steps down again and analysts cut estimates and targets. Lithium equities may also keep trending with GFEX futures, and there is no stated timeline for a price floor.
- The bull case is that the business is still highly profitable at current prices, with Q3 EBITDA margin near 49%. Management says capex is unchanged and prices are below the incentive level. The stock is at about 10 times earnings and near multi-month lows, and Chinese spot has bounced for two days.
- Catalysts to watch are GFEX lithium carbonate direction, post-earnings analyst target cuts, and Albemarle and peer action.

**Gaps.** I did not find post-earnings analyst actions, SQM's current options positioning, or the Q4 consensus EPS. Bloomberg and Citi's article were blocked (403). The Seeking Alpha article was cut off. SQM's claimed 2026 price floor of $15–18/kg comes from an unconfirmed blog.

agents.report:
**FE research summary, as of 12:20 PM CT Wednesday 2026-11-18.** I found no fresh company-specific catalyst today. The move looks like technical and sector-driven buying on top of a solid fundamental story. Some search-result dates and figures conflicted, and I note where that matters.

**What the move looks like**
- FE crossed above its 200-day average (about $47.50) on Monday 11/17 on roughly 4.4M shares, per [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-firstenergy-nyse-fe-shares-cross-above-two-hundred-day-moving-average-time-to-sell-2026-11-17/). Its 50-day average is about $45.54.
- Morningstar showed about $47.56 midday, up about 1%, against $47.06 the prior close ([Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/xnys/fe/quote)).
- The 52-week range is roughly $42.67 to $52.34, with a September low of $43.72. FE is mid-range and bouncing off lows.
- I found no news dated today. Local press releases only: a foundation hire and Lakewood transformer work ([FirstEnergy](https://www.firstenergycorp.com/fehome.html)).
- The 2.1 times volume is therefore best explained by the 200-day breakout and sector flows, not a company event.

**Fundamentals**
- Q3 results (Oct 27): Core EPS was $0.98 against about $0.90 consensus, and revenue was $4.56B against $4.24B expected ([8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031296/000103129626000142/ex991-q32026newsrelease.htm)).
- 2026 Core EPS guidance of $2.62 to $2.82 was reaffirmed, with results at or slightly above the $2.72 midpoint. Core growth is expected near the top of 6% to 8% through 2030.
- Year-to-date Core EPS of $2.20 is up 9%.
- The capital plan is $36B over five years. Rate base grew 9.9% and transmission rate base grew 14%. Trailing-12-month ROE is 9.5% ([call summary](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262247883-tradingkey)).
- Weather-adjusted load rose 1.2% for a fourth straight positive quarter. Industrial load rose 3.3%.
- Data centers: 7.9 GW is under contract, up about 90% since the start of 2026, with about 4 GW more in negotiation. West Virginia pipeline is nearly 6 GW.
- The transmission plan is $19B today and management expects at least a 25% increase with the roll-forward. Their rule of thumb is about $250M of network upgrades per GW.
- Equity needs are modest: up to $2B through 2030, around 1% of market cap per year, and about 35% equity funding on the Maidsville project.
- Valuation: P/E is about 22.9, beta 0.39, and the dividend is $1.86 a year (about 3.9% yield). The ex-dividend date was Nov 6 and payment is Dec 1, so there is no dividend event in the window.

**Analysts**
- Consensus is Moderate Buy, with 8 Buy and 4 Hold and an average target of about $50.77. Aggregators range from $50.64 to $50.77.
- October brought mixed target changes:
  - Barclays: $54 to $49, Overweight.
  - BofA: $53 to $47, Neutral.
  - JPMorgan: $52 to $50, Neutral.
  - Morgan Stanley: $49 to $50, Overweight.
  - HSBC initiated at Buy, $50.
- Jefferies has a Hold. Source: [coverage roundup](https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/quote/FE/analyst-insights/).
- The stock at $47.7 sits below the consensus target, but the targets are mostly cluster-flat, not a strong upgrade cycle.

**Regulatory calendar**

| Item | Status and timing |
|---|---|
| West Virginia Maidsville gas plant | Roughly $2.4B to $2.7B and about 1,200 MW (figures vary by source). The certificate order is expected in Q4 2026. Public comment in July drew broad opposition, and consumer groups call it speculative ([Dominion Post](https://www.dominionpost.com/2026/07/16/proposed-firstenergy-gas-fired-power-plant-draws-universal-opposition-at-public-hearing/), [Utility Dive](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/firstenergy-data-center-west-virginia-maidsville-earnings/826558/)). This is the largest event risk in the window, and the order could land any day before year-end. |
| West Virginia $76M adjustment | Approved as filed, with a stay-out through April 2028. |
| Ohio distribution case | Asks for about $400M to $481M on a 10.20% ROE, with new rates in mid-2027. The staff report is due Nov 30, objections come around year-end, a public hearing is Dec 17 and the evidentiary hearing is in March. The staff report is a possible near-term catalyst. The last Ohio case saw staff recommend only $8.5M against $190M requested ([Ohio Capital Journal](https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2026/10/28/price-hikes-arent-all-thats-at-stake-in-firstenergy-ohios-rate-case/), [S&P](https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/06/firstenergy-ohio-rate-plan-seeks-400m-of-new-revenue-2b-of-added-rate-base)). |
| New Jersey | $253M request, clarity expected late 2026 or early 2027. |
| Maryland | $53M request, hearings in January and an outcome in April 2027. |
| Pennsylvania | The default-service order passed 3-2 on Oct 22. The PUC rejected FirstEnergy's request to return customers to default service at contract expiration. The Consumer Advocate filed for reconsideration on Nov 9 ([PUC filing](https://www.puc.pa.gov/pcdocs/1958492.pdf)). |

- Management also said it wants any federal rule on data-center transmission costs to assign them to data centers. It opposes taking generation commodity risk in PJM's backstop procurement.
- PJM's 2028/29 capacity auction (July) cleared at the $325/MW-day cap with a 6,831 MW shortfall. The price cap covers one more auction (2029/30). Source: [PJM report](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/markets-ops/rpm/rpm-auction-info/2028-2029/2028-2029-bra-results-report.pdf). The affordability politics around that shortfall are a regulatory overhang for Mid-Atlantic utilities.
- Other dates: Q4 results and the 2027 to 2031 plan arrive in February 2027. A West Virginia request for proposals for 3 GW of turbines should update in early 2027.

**Legacy overhang (low impact now)**
- The SEC and the shareholder derivative suits are resolved.
- Ohio approved a roughly $275M customer restitution settlement in January 2026.
- Former executives Jones and Dowling were reindicted, with jury selection reported for Jan 21, 2027. This is a headline risk only. One timeline entry carried a date after today, so treat that source cautiously ([Common Cause timeline](https://www.commoncause.org/ohio/resources/a-cycle-of-corruption-a-timeline-of-the-householder-hb6-scandal/)).

**Credit and macro**
- Moody's moved its outlook to positive in March, Fitch affirmed in September, and credit facilities were extended in October.
- Utilities were reported as very oversold in early October ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/etf/2026/10/02/utility-stocks-are-the-most-oversold-since-2023/)). XLU is about $43 to $44, against a 52-week range of $39 to $47.80.
- One commentary said the 10-year yield is back above 5% and a December Fed hike is possible. That is a headwind for utilities, but I could not confirm it from a second source. XLU's 11/17 move was also unclear, with sources giving conflicting numbers.

**Takeaway for a 1 to 10 session trade**
- **For:** The earnings beat and reaffirmed guidance, the data-center and transmission growth story, and the 200-day reclaim with a rising 50-day average. The stock is still below the average analyst target, and low beta and a manageable equity need limit funding risk.
- **Against:**
  - The stock is only about 2.5% above its 200-day average and has limited headroom to the mid-$50s.
  - The 50-day is still below the 200-day.
  - A rate shock could hit utilities as a group.
  - The Maidsville order has binary risk. The WV PSC has shown it scrutinizes FirstEnergy's generation plans, but the other WV adjustment was approved.
- **Window catalysts:** the Maidsville certificate order (any day, Q4), the Ohio staff report (by Nov 30), and the Pennsylvania reconsideration.
- **Where the story could break:** a Maidsville rejection or onerous conditions, a harsh Ohio staff report, a rate spike, or a failed hold of the $47.50 area.

agents.report:
**Newmont (NEM) research, 12:20 PM CT, Wednesday 2026-11-18**

**Summary.** Today's drop looks like a macro move in gold, not a company problem. NEM is down about 6.7% at 103.8, in line with a 2.8% fall in gold. There is no Newmont-specific news today. The company's last report (October 22) was strong. The trade comes down to whether gold bottoms, and the next catalysts are today's Fed minutes and the December 9 Fed decision.

**What happened today**
- Spot gold fell 2% to 2.8% to about $3,745–3,770, touching $3,757 earlier. That is its lowest since September 2025 and more than 30% below the January record near $5,600. COMEX futures hit about $3,745. ([FXStreet](https://fxstreet.com/news/gold-tumbles-to-its-lowest-in-over-a-year-as-fed-rate-hike-bets-build-202611181109), [CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/18/stocks-moving-the-most-today-live-updates.html))
- The cause is Fed hike expectations and a strong dollar. A December hike is fully priced, with about 70% odds of another in January. The dollar index is near 103.8, the highest since April 2025, and the 10-year Treasury yield is above 5%. Governor Waller floated a 50bp move. ([FXStreet](https://fxstreet.com/news/gold-tumbles-to-its-lowest-in-over-a-year-as-fed-rate-hike-bets-build-202611181109))
- Silver fell 4.9% to about $45. AngloGold Ashanti fell nearly 8%, and Freeport-McMoRan and Southern Copper were also down. Oil fell 4.5% and the energy sector fell nearly 3%. ([CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/18/stocks-moving-the-most-today-live-updates.html))
- Seeking Alpha's headline has Newmont down almost 8% at about 12:42 PM ET. I could not open the article, so I only have the headline and snippet. ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4674320-newmont-slumps-8-amid-broad-losses-among-gold-peers))
- StockAnalysis showed 103.83, down 6.68% from the 111.26 prior close. NEM has a beta of 0.56 and is falling about 2.4 times as hard as gold today. ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nem/))

**Catalysts**
- **Today, 2:00 PM ET (1:00 PM CT):** minutes of the October Fed meeting. Hawkish minutes would confirm the hike path. Balanced minutes could pull hike expectations down. With a December hike already about 98% priced, one source argues the downside surprise is limited. That source is promotional-leaning. ([TradingNEWS](https://www.tradingnews.com/news/gold-xau-usd-breaks-3800-to-14-month-low-3757-reclaiming-3890-puts-4050-usd-target-in-play))
- **Nov 25:** NEM goes ex-dividend, $0.26 a share (about 1% yield). ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nem/))
- **Late November:** October PCE inflation, and November CPI around early December.
- **Dec 9:** Fed decision.
- **Q4 results:** about late February. The February dividend review is expected to raise the dividend to about $0.27.
- **Q4 cost guide:** Q4 all-in sustaining cost is guided to about $1,900 an ounce, the year's highest, so the next report may look worse on costs.

**Newmont fundamentals (Q3 report, Oct 22)**
- Adjusted EPS was $2.20 against a $1.94 consensus. Adjusted net income was $2.3B, adjusted EBITDA $4.0B and free cash flow $1.9B for the quarter ($7.26B year to date). The realized gold price was $4,317 an ounce, so a $3,750 gold price is about 13% below what Q3 earned. ([Newmont release](https://www.newmont.com/investors/news-release/news-details/2026/Newmont-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-with-Record-Third-Quarter-Adjusted-Net-Income-Positioned-to-Achieve-Full-Year-Guidance-Provides-Update-on-Red-Chris-Block-Cave-Project/default.aspx))
- Full-year production guidance is about 5.3 million ounces, with Q4 expected to be the strongest quarter. Full-year all-in sustaining cost guidance improved to about $1,520 an ounce, about 10% better than the original.
- Cash is $8.8B and net cash $3.2B. A $1.95B payment to Barrick for the Nevada Gold Mines (NGM) amendment is due in Q4 and will reduce that. The amendment adds Fourmile, Fiberline and Mike.
- Buybacks were $1.6B since the last call, with $2.8B left of the $6B program. More than 10% of shares have been retired since February 2024. Buybacks are a possible support, but the company has not committed to buying on dips.
- A $100 an ounce change in gold moves revenue and costs by about $505M. The valuation is about 12 times trailing earnings and 11.35 times forward earnings. ([Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/22/newmont-nem-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))

**Company-specific risks**
- **Lihir (Papua New Guinea):** El Niño water shortages could hurt Q4 production and costs. I found no confirmation of an actual shortage yet.
- **Peñasquito:** silver output is expected to roughly halve in Q4 and fall about 30% in 2027.
- **2027 costs:** unit costs are expected to rise on inflation, diesel, the Australian dollar and gold-linked royalties. Production is guided up low-to-mid single digits. Development capex is up about $500M.
- **Cadia:** the PC1-2 cave establishment is about six months behind after an April seismic event.
- **Red Chris block cave:** capex is $4.2–4.8B, well above earlier estimates. A funding decision is due in early 2027, with first production in 2033. A Canadian government grant of about C$500M is still being finalized.
- **Ahafo North:** the ramp-up was softer than analysts expected.
- **Tanami:** Expansion 2 is now expected in the first half of 2027.

**Analysts**
- Consensus is "Buy" or "Moderate Buy," with an average target of about $135–137 (MarketBeat: 25 firms, 19 Buy, 2 Strong Buy, 4 Hold, no Sell). ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/consensus-newmont-corporation-nem-what-are-brokerages-saying-about-this-stock-2026-11-18/))
- Recent target changes include Jefferies to $149 from $155 on Nov 17, RBC at $155, Scotiabank at $148, BMO at $145, Citi and BofA at $140, and BNP at $112 (Neutral).
- Freedom Broker downgraded the stock to Hold on Oct 22, with a $115–116 target. That is the only downgrade I found.
- These targets predate today's gold drop and will likely be revised.

**Technicals and ownership**
- The 50-day average was $117.33 and the 200-day $112.15 before today. Today's price is below both.
- The 12-month range is $81.34 to $135.29. The stock is about 23% below the high and 28% above the low.
- CEO Viljoen sold 3,882 shares on Sep 1 at $123, and EVP Toth sold 3,000 on Nov 2 at $108.04. Both sales were under pre-arranged 10b5-1 plans, so they carry little signal.

**Gold levels to watch**
- Resistance is $3,800, then $3,853 (Tuesday's close) and $3,890. A daily close above $3,890 would suggest a false breakdown.
- Support is $3,700, then $3,570–3,600.
- The relative strength index (RSI) is about 32, near oversold.
- The 10-year yield above 5.15% points toward $3,700 and then $3,600. A dollar index close below 103 would signal a dollar reversal.
- One source says miners rising while gold is still falling would be an early bottoming sign.
- Chinese central bank buying continues (25.8 tonnes in October, the 24th straight month). ([TradingNEWS](https://www.tradingnews.com/news/gold-xau-usd-breaks-3800-to-14-month-low-3757-reclaiming-3890-puts-4050-usd-target-in-play))

**Caveats**
- Search results gave conflicting numbers on whether the Fed target range and hikes are as stated. I relied on the Nov 18 FXStreet and TradingNEWS pieces.
- Several pages returned 403 errors: Seeking Alpha, EBC, Kalkine and Alphastreet. Their claims are not verified.
- Some Newmont and Freedom Broker pieces were undated.
- I could not confirm any Newmont-specific news today. Searches for new Newmont news returned only stale items, so repeated searching stopped surfacing anything new. I found no short interest, options or ETF-flow data.

**For the 1–10 session decision.** Gold sits on an oversold, mostly priced-in hike path, so a bounce is plausible, but today's rate-driven selling has momentum. Gold has fallen below its prior lows, and Newmont is about 12 times earnings with a strong Q3 report behind it. The first Newmont-specific event is the Nov 25 ex-dividend date.

**Bottom line.** The ADR has fallen about 64% from its 52-week high of $21.29, with no company-specific shock behind today's move. I found three things driving it today:
- Metals are being sold on Fed rate-hike fears.
- A $500M convertible bond redemption was announced today and will dilute shares.
- The US PGM operations are still recovering from a strike.

I found no news from today that undermines the South African business. The Fed minutes at 1:00 PM CT could move metals again within the hour.

**1. Metals selloff (the main driver).**
- October CPI came in hot at +0.4% against +0.3% expected. The market now prices about a 95% chance of a 25 bp hike at the Dec 8-9 Fed meeting.
- The dollar index is near 103.7, close to a 19-month high. The 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.1%.
- Spot gold is down about 2.1% to roughly $3,770, the lowest since September 2025. It fell below $4,000 on Nov 11 and has slid since. The peak this year was about $5,318 on Jan 29.
- Platinum is down about 3.4% to roughly $1,382, the lowest since late September 2025 and down about 30% this year. The 2026 high was $2,735 on Jan 23.
- Palladium is down about 2.2% to roughly $950. Silver is down about 3.4% to roughly $45.8.
- The Fed's Oct 27-28 meeting minutes come out at 1:00 PM CT. They could reinforce the hawkish tone or ease it.
- US-Iran tensions and Hormuz attacks are not supporting gold, because rates and the dollar are dominating.

**2. Convertible bond redemption (the most likely company-specific piece today).**
- Today, Stillwater Mining Company, Sibanye's US subsidiary, called its $500M 4.25% convertible bonds due 2028. The notice is dated Nov 18 in Johannesburg, so it likely landed before the US open.
- Holders can convert until Dec 11. Anything not converted is repaid in cash at par on Dec 21.
- If all holders convert, up to 398,946,781 new ordinary shares are issued. Against about 2.83B shares outstanding, that is roughly 14% dilution.
- One German report quotes a conversion price of $1.2533 per ordinary share. One ADR is 4 ordinary shares (my recollection, not confirmed in these sources), so that is about $5 per ADR. With the ADR at $7.76, holders are well in the money and will almost certainly convert.
- The company frames this as gross-debt reduction. The bond helped fund the 2023 Reldan recycling acquisition.
- The same German report says the stock fell 5.8% on announcement day and that its last EUR quote was down 7.19%.
- The 2023 bond launch caused a drop of more than 25% in the JSE shares. Citi called it an "acquisition risk overhang."
- Bondholders often hedge by shorting the stock. Redemption could therefore bring some forced selling or hedge unwinding between now and Dec 11. That is my inference, not something a source stated.

**3. US PGM strike aftermath.** This was news on Nov 5.
- A strike ran from Sept 3 to Oct 9 at the Stillwater mine and the Columbus complex.
- 2026 US output guidance was cut to 245-255k oz, from 280-300k oz. All-in sustaining cost guidance rose to $1,700-1,760/oz, from $1,520-1,580.
- Q3 US output fell 19% to 59,417 oz. Unit cost rose 39% to $1,617/oz.
- Staffing is about 25% below the planned 2027 mechanised workforce. Q4 is a rebuild quarter, and the full sales impact lands in Q4.
- The new labour deal includes a 4.5% first-year raise.
- Long-term targets are about $1,000/oz unit cost by end-2028 and about 410k oz of annual output.
- The US business is the only part of the group guided to miss 2026 targets. South African operations are on track.
- The stock fell about 3.6% on Nov 12 on weaker PGM prices.

**4. Fundamentals, which are strong on paper but priced at peak-cycle metals.**
- Q3 adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to R10.8bn. The first half had revenue of about R90bn, up 64%, and adjusted EBITDA of R31.8bn, up more than double.
- Net debt is about R9.7bn. That is 0.18x EBITDA, against gross borrowings of R32.1bn and cash of R22.4bn. Liquidity is R47.6bn.
- The interim dividend was 201 cents per share (about R5.7bn), paid in September. StockAnalysis shows an ADR dividend of $0.80, a 10% yield. That is a trailing figure that depends on metal prices, and the payout could be lower next time if prices stay down.
- Keliber, the Finnish lithium project, is over budget at €783m against €588m. Its refinery commissioning decision is due in Q4 and depends on lithium prices. Management flagged a bigger-than-expected lithium surplus.
- Other items: the Burnstone restart, the K4 shaft ramp-up at Marikana, Siphumelele UG2 phase 1, and JPMorgan disclosing a 5.22% stake on Nov 16.

agents.report:
**KGC research as of 12:30 PM CT, Wednesday 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line:** Today's drop looks like a gold-driven selloff on a stock already damaged by its own news. I found no new Kinross-specific news today. The stock has now fallen through the low it set in the weeks after its September guidance cut.

**Why it's down today**
- Gold is the main driver today.
  - Spot gold fell below $3,800, the first time since September 2025. It reached about $3,770, down about 2% from yesterday.
  - December COMEX gold futures fell as much as 3.1%.
  - The stated causes are hawkish Fed talk and a firmer dollar.
  - St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said "several" more hikes are likely.
  - Markets price quarter-point hikes in December and January. The current range is 3.75-4.00%.
  - The 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.1%.
  - The dollar index is at 103.65, its highest since April 2025.
  - Gold is about 32% below its January 29 record of $5,595.
  - GLD closed Tuesday at $352.48, down 11% year to date.
- Miners were already falling before today.
  - From November 6 to 16, Agnico Eagle fell 10.8%, Barrick 10.0% and Newmont 8.8%. That is about double gold's own decline.
  - GDX was about 31% below its February record close.
  - Kinross has beta of about 2 (MarketBeat), so a 2-3% gold drop producing a 6.5% share drop fits.
- I did not find an account of today's moves in other gold miners.

**The Kinross story**
1. **Round Mountain guidance cut (Sept 23).**
   - Kinross cut its 2026 and 2027 output outlook from roughly 2.0 million ounces to 1.84-1.86 million. That is 8-9% below consensus, per one law-firm release.
   - Causes were ore recovery and grade problems at Round Mountain (Nevada) and, per management, weather and copper-in-ore issues at La Coipa (Chile).
   - The stock fell about 11.6%, from $27.62 to $24.42.
   - Management called it "a deferral as opposed to a loss." Jefferies agreed that much of the volume looks deferred.
   - Analysts had pressed Round Mountain issues since April (Stifel and Canaccord, per a law-firm release).
2. **Q3 results (Oct 28) were mixed.**
   - Production was 424.7k ounces versus 503.9k a year earlier. Cost of sales was $1,485 per ounce versus $1,145. All-in sustaining cost (AISC) was $1,947 versus $1,622.
   - Realized gold was $4,249 per ounce. The margin was still about $2,747 per ounce, and adjusted EPS was $0.50.
   - Free cash flow was weak: $281M attributable. Capex was $440M. Cash is $2.6B and net cash is $1.9B.
   - The capital-return target rose from 40% to 50% of free cash flow. Buybacks were about $230M in Q3, and over $950M has been returned year to date. The year-to-date buyback figure is stated inconsistently in the release, at $710M and $810M.
   - Guidance was reaffirmed. Round Mountain recovery was 60% versus 44% the prior quarter, with a target of about 80% late in the year.
   - Great Bear first gold is targeted for 2029, Round Mountain Phase X for 2028, and Lobo-Marte for the early 2030s.
3. **Securities class action.**
   - It was filed November 9 in Colorado, with a class period of February 18 to September 23. It alleges the company's "on track for 2 million ounces" statements were misleading.
   - The lead plaintiff deadline is January 5, 2027.
   - These are plaintiff-firm advertisements and the allegations are unproven. I found no Kinross response. It is a headline and overhang rather than a near-term cash event.
4. **Analysts are mostly still positive but trimming.**
   - Consensus is Buy, with an average target of $37.98 (MarketBeat). Targets were cut in September and October, for example National Bank from C$42.50 to C$40.
   - Seeking Alpha contributors moved to Hold or Sell. One preferred Barrick, with a $20 target. I could not open that article.

**Setup facts**
- On the TSX the stock hit a C$26.90 low. It had closed Tuesday at C$28.80.
- The TSX 50-day average is C$33.75 and the 200-day is C$38.83.
- The stock trades at about 10 times earnings in Canadian terms (MarketBeat), and the market cap is about C$32B.
- The dividend is $0.04 per share, with an ex-dividend date of Thursday, November 19. That is about 0.2% and does not matter for a trade.
- Goldman cut its end-2026 gold target to $4,150 from $4,650. It still expects prices above current levels and cites central-bank buying of about 60 tonnes a month.

**Catalysts in the 1-10 session window**
- **Fed minutes from the October meeting, today at 2:00 PM ET (1:00 PM CT).** This is about 30 minutes from now. A dovish read could reverse the selloff. A hawkish read could push gold toward $3,700, then $3,605 (the World Gold Council's reference level).
- **Fed decision on December 8-9.** A hike is largely priced in.
- **Dollar index and Treasury yields.** One article's bullish-reversal signal is spot gold closing back above $3,800 with the dollar index below 103.65.
- **Kinross-specific:** I found no scheduled catalysts apart from the lawsuit deadline on January 5.

**Read for the trade**
- Bear case: momentum in gold, rate-hike expectations and a rising dollar all point the wrong way. Miners have levered gold's decline, and there is no support level yet since the stock is at 52-week lows.
- Bull case: the guidance cut is already priced in, and guidance was reaffirmed in Q3. Net cash is $1.9B with 50% of free cash flow going back to holders. The selloff in gold and the miners looks extended, which sets up a bounce if the minutes or the dollar turn.
- The result is likely to follow gold day to day. The Fed minutes decide the next move.

**Caveats**
- Quoted prices conflict across sources. MarketBeat's $19.94 and $22.21 do not match each other.
- The Benzinga and Motley Fool transcripts did not open. Benzinga returned a 403.
- Invezz, Seeking Alpha and some other sites were blocked.
- I did not find the pre-market note that the Tiger article referenced, and could not confirm its date.
- Searches stopped turning up new Kinross items, but I found no coverage from today beyond law-firm press releases and the MarketBeat 52-week-low note.

**RLI (RLI): research summary as of 2026-11-18, about 12:30 PM CT**

**Bottom line:** I found no news catalyst for today's move. The stock has rallied about 29% in seven weeks on a clean Q3 beat and a second special dividend. The sell side doesn't support the new price. The $3.00 special dividend goes ex on Mon 2026-11-30, which is the 7th session after today and inside a 1-10 session hold. Expect the price to be marked down about $3, or 4.2% of 71.43, that day.

**The story**
- RLI is a specialty insurer in Casualty, Property and Surety. It reported Q3 on Oct 19.
  - Operating EPS was $0.86 against a $0.51 consensus, up from $0.82 a year earlier.
  - The combined ratio was 86.2, against 85.1 a year earlier.
  - Gross premiums written rose only 2%, to $522.2M.
  - Net investment income rose 13% to $46.7M, with new money yielding about 5.5%.
  - Operating cash flow was $195M and trailing return on equity about 22%.
- The beat leaned on favorable prior-year reserve development of about $20-23M. The two sources give different totals ($20.1M of net underwriting benefit vs. $22.9M).
- Segment combined ratios:
  - Property was 60.1 and carries the profit.
  - Surety was 79.8.
  - Casualty was 99.6, with almost no margin and underwriting income of just $1.0M against $4.5M a year earlier.
- Management says three-quarters of full-year underwriting profit is already booked. There was no formal guidance.
- Premium trends by line:
  - Personal umbrella premium rose 22%, with rates up 8%. Management expects double-digit rate increases to return in 2027.
  - Hawaii homeowners rose 9%.
  - Marine rose 11%.
  - Surety rose about 1%.
  - E&S property fell 17%, and renewal rates fell by double digits. Management expects more softening.
  - E&S casualty fell 10%.
  - Commercial transportation fell 9%, with renewal retention down almost 10 points as returning MGAs compete for large accounts.
- Management says it will shrink rather than chase price. Surety competitors are loosening terms, and excess casualty is crowded with MGAs and standard carriers, especially in the Northeast.
- The Steadily landlord-insurance distribution partnership (from April 2026) added about $9M of premium in Q3. It carries a higher commission cost.
- Industry backdrop is soft:
  - WTW says specialty rates are falling faster in 2026 than in 2025, with property down 17% net of trend.
  - Swiss Re sees underwriting margins shrinking from 4.4% to 1.7% in 2027.
  - Offsetting that, management expects a buyer's market in reinsurance for the 2027 renewals, which would cut RLI's reinsurance costs.

**Capital return**
- On Nov 11 the board declared a $3.00 special dividend (about $275M) plus the regular $0.18. Both are payable Dec 7 to holders of record Nov 30.
- The release doesn't state an ex-dividend date. With T+1 settlement it should be Nov 30, and the last cum-dividend day should be Fri Nov 27 (check with your broker).
- A $2.00 special was also paid in June 2026 (record date May 29).
- $231.7M remains on the buyback authorization. Q3 repurchases were small: 103,573 shares at $60.51.
- The 51-year streak of regular dividend increases continues.

**Price and sentiment**
- The stock closed May 29 at about $50.82 (Digrin's ex-date close, after the $2 special).
- Aug 25: the stock fell about 3% to $64.54 on the Jefferies downgrade.
- Sep 8: $61.14. The Q3 release shows a 9/30 close of $55.31, which looks inconsistent with the $58-61 prices elsewhere and may be wrong.
- After Q3 it hit new 52-week highs of $67.28 on Oct 22 and $67.28 again around Nov 2.
- A 52-week high of $71.89-71.90 appears on Nov 12-17, so today's 71.43 is at or just below the intraday high. Robinhood shows a Nov 17 range of $70.24-71.09.
- Analysts:
  - Jefferies cut to Underperform with a $53 target on Aug 25. It cited roughly 3x book value, operating return on equity near 13%, and little room for error. Its 2026-28 EPS estimates sit about 7% below consensus.
  - Wells Fargo is Underweight with a $53 target.
  - Keefe, Bruyette & Woods is Outperform with a $74 target, raised from $69 on Oct 21.
  - UBS has a $74 target.
  - MarketBeat shows a consensus of "Reduce" (1 Buy, 3 Hold, 2 Sell) with a $62.40 target. Benzinga shows $71 across 12 analysts. The sources conflict.
- Valuation: P/E about 20 and beta 0.31. Market cap is about $6.3B.
- The price is well above the $62.40 MarketBeat consensus target and above all but the two $74 targets.

**Setup for 1-10 sessions**
- The case for trading it:
  - Momentum plus a rising 50-day average (61.26) over the 200-day (59.07).
  - Low beta.
  - Dividend-capture-style buying into Nov 27.
  - Possible tax-loss-season rotation into defensive names.
- The case against:

  - The special dividend produces a mechanical ~4.2% gap down on Nov 30, so a hold through that date needs more than a 4% gain first.

  - Fundamentals are softening in the high-margin property line.

**Automakers and parts (F, GM, APTV): research report, 12:30 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line:** I found no single catalyst for today's basket weakness. The ordinary sector story explains the 5.7% slide over 20 sessions. The backdrop is soft and the stocks are cheap, but nothing identifiable should snap back within 1-10 sessions. I couldn't find any news from today on F, GM or APTV, nor anything on why APTV is up 2.2% against GM at -0.6%. Treat that split as unexplained, not as a signal.

**What the web did and didn't show**
- I didn't find a dated news item that moves any of the three today.
- Search results were thin and sometimes contradictory. Where sources conflict, I say so below.
- I couldn't read the Stockopedia item about a possible 82% USMCA regional-content rule (page came back empty). Its date and substance are unconfirmed. I can't say it is current or that it moved anything today.

**Ford (F), about $11.5-12**
- Price: it closed $11.91 on Nov 13, then fell 2.9% to about $11.57 on Nov 16 (low $11.48). That is below the 50-day average (about $12.56) and the 200-day (about $13.30), and about 7% down year to date.
- Q3 (Oct 28): adjusted EPS $0.49 vs about $0.41 expected, and adjusted free cash flow $4.7B, roughly $2B above estimates. Revenue of about $49.5B was down about 2%, with Blue, Pro and Model e all missing revenue estimates.
- 2026 guidance: adjusted EBIT narrowed to $10.5-11B (low end raised from $10B), and free cash flow held at $6-7B. Ford Pro was cut to about $7B, the bottom of its range, on commodities and Oakville launch costs. Model e is still losing about $4B.
- Supplier fire: Novelis' Oswego aluminum plant (Sept 16) cost Ford about $1B in temporary costs year to date, with more in Q4. Management says operational recovery is "largely behind us."
- 2027: management expects earnings roughly flat versus 2026. A $1.3B tariff refund in Q1 2026 is offset by aluminum sourcing costs that won't repeat. Farley calls 2027 a "foundational year" toward an 8% margin by 2029.
- Dividend: $0.15 per quarter, ex-date Nov 10 (already passed), payable Dec 1. That is about $0.60 a year, a yield near 5.2%, and 20% below 2025's $0.75 because no supplemental was paid.
- Analysts: consensus is Hold (7 Buy, 11 Hold, 1 Sell), average target about $15. Recent cuts include Goldman to $12 (neutral), RBC to $14 and BNP to $13. Beta is 1.88.
- Technical: commentary says a break below $12 leaves $10 as the next round-number target.

**General Motors (GM), about $84**
- Price: $84.01 at 1:02 PM ET today, near flat, in a day range of $83.04-85.02. Its 52-week range is $67.61-93.70. It was about $86.60 around Nov 12.
- Nasdaq switch: GM moved from the NYSE to the Nasdaq on Nov 17 (ticker unchanged).
  - The point is Nasdaq-100 eligibility, which would force buying by funds tracking the index. Eligibility is ranked on the last trading day of November, and changes are typically announced in mid-December.
  - Last year's Walmart switch drew an estimated $19B of index buying. Nothing is official, and the Motley Fool author calls it a short-term catalyst at best.
- Q3 (Oct 20): revenue about $50B and adjusted EBIT about $4.1B (up about 22%). EV realignment charges were only $238M, versus $1.6B a year earlier, with about $1B more expected in Q4.
- 2026 guidance: adjusted EBIT $14.5-15.5B (narrowed), and automotive free cash flow raised to $11.5-12.5B. A new $20B buyback has no expiry, and management gave no cadence for it.
- Stock reaction to the print: one source says the stock fell despite higher profits, on concern about costs and pricing next year. Other results from older GM earnings coverage cite a jump of 6-15%, and I couldn't reconcile them. I didn't pin down the Oct 20 close.
- Other: reported plans to raise factory automation by 20% by 2028 (Reuters, Nov 17).

**Aptiv (APTV), about $44-45 before today's move**
- Structure: the electrical distribution business was spun off as Versigent (VGNT) on April 1, 2026. APTV is now a smaller, higher-margin company, and several sources describe a post-spin re-rating. The price level is well below the roughly $59 seen in July.
- Q3 (Nov 3): adjusted EPS $1.42 vs about $1.33-1.35 expected, revenue $3.2B (about 2% growth, slight miss), and adjusted EBITDA margin 18% (down 140 bps). Non-auto revenue grew 11% and auto fell 1%.
- 2026 guidance: adjusted EPS $5.60-5.80 held, with the free-cash-flow midpoint trimmed $25M to $650M.
- Buybacks: at least $650M by year-end, and 100% of free cash flow returned through at least 2027.
- Reaction: the stock moved only modestly (premarket roughly +0.5% in one source, about -3% in another). It was about $44 on Nov 2-3.
- 2027 outlook (preliminary): management called it "intentionally conservative" and assumes flat global vehicle production.
  - About $700M of year-over-year chip and memory cost increases in 2027, mostly memory. Management says recoveries from customers are EBITDA-neutral but dilute margin percentages.
  - A European revenue drag of $250-300M from two German luxury automakers, lasting through 2027.
  - A portfolio and product review, with an update in Q1 2027.
- Memory: the AI-driven memory shortage is a real industry headwind (automotive DRAM prices reportedly up as much as 180% in three months, per an August report). This is APTV's main stated risk and also a possible production risk for F and GM.
- Analyst targets: dated and conflicting. UBS cut to $80 and RBC to $81 after the spin, and Goldman initiated at $74 in April. No November analyst action was found.
- Context: it lagged badly (about -24% over three months to late October), so today's +2.2% is a bounce from a depressed level.

**Sector backdrop**
- Affordability: Cox Automotive put the typical new-vehicle payment at $776 in September, the highest since December 2023, with an average transaction price of $50,562. This is the main fundamental worry in the reports I found.
- Policy: Section 232 auto tariffs of 25% remain (15% for the EU, Japan and Korea), and the USMCA review is live. The 232 tariffs are expected to be negotiated, and the US is expected to push tougher rules of origin. A detailed November status wasn't found.
- Today: XLY is strong on retail earnings. A basket down 1.5% against it is partly a rotation out of autos, not necessarily autos-specific news.

**For the journal (1-10 sessions)**
- Bearish case: both detroit names are below their 50-day averages with Ford near a break of support, there is no near-term catalyst for the group, affordability is worsening, and today's drop is mostly relative to a strong XLY.

- Dated catalysts: GM's Nasdaq-100 ranking on the last trading day of November, with an announcement likely mid-December, and the Ford dividend on Dec 1. I found no earnings in the window. The next ones are in January.
- Basket mechanics: GM and F, the two larger names, are the weak ones, and APTV is the only one up. The basket signal here is about the two OEMs, not parts.

agents.report:
**Bottom line:** VALE is falling mostly because of the iron ore price, with a risk-off, rising-yield tape adding to it. I found no company-specific shock. The stretch is genuine, but I found no catalyst that says the selling is done. Today's (Nov 18) move is not directly documented anywhere I could reach.

**Why the stock is falling**
- **Iron ore at four-year lows.**
  - Dalian futures hit about 647.5 yuan/t and Singapore about $87.85/t on Nov 16, the weakest since Nov 2022.
  - Today (Nov 18) they bounced slightly, to about $87.75 in Singapore and 649 yuan in Dalian, still at or near the lows.
  - Demand is soft: China's October steel output was 70.83 Mt, the lowest since March. October industrial output, retail sales and fixed-asset investment all missed.
  - Port stocks are heavy. One source (Discovery Alert, early Nov) put imported ore at about 173 Mt at 47 ports. Another source (Bloomberg/Edge Singapore, Nov 18) put it at 152 Mt at 35 ports.
  - Supply is rising, including Simandou. Macquarie expects global supply up about 14 Mt in 2026.
- **Macro.**
  - Rio Times wrote that markets expect a Fed hike in December. It cited Polymarket at 91.5%, a 10-year yield near 5.1% and a VIX near 23.
  - The odds I found in other sources ranged from 70% to 84%, and I couldn't date them. Treat the exact figure as unconfirmed.
- **Vale's Q3 (reported Oct 29).**
  - Pro forma EBITDA was $3.5B, down 20% year on year. The realized iron ore price was $85.1/t.
  - All-in iron ore cost was $60.40/t, up 21% year on year.
  - Iron ore output fell 6%. Vale said it will only reach the low end of its 335–345 Mt guidance.
  - Management said an extra dividend is unlikely and no buyback ran in Q3.
  - Base metals were the bright spot, with EBITDA up more than 60% to about $1.1B. Copper all-in cost was negative $200/t.
  - Net debt was $16.4B, within Vale's $10–20B target range. Free cash flow was $2.2B.
  - More than 80% of 2027 freight is hedged. Management said about 160 Mt of seaborne supply is loss-making at current prices.
- **Analysts.**
  - UBS cut its target to $13.50 from $14.50 and stayed neutral (Nov 2).
  - The consensus is Hold with an average target around $15.6, which is stale against a $10 stock.
  - BofA, Goldman and Morgan Stanley cut to neutral over July and August.

**The stock's own path**
- It fell 6.77% on Nov 16 to $10.46, then 0.38% to $10.42 on Nov 17, a fourth straight down day and a 12-month low.
- That is about 41% below the April high of $17.82.
- Note that Rio Times' Nov 16 article quotes -12.61% over 5 sessions and -20.21% over 20, identical to your screen's figures. The screen's data may be lagging, or the 5- and 20-session figures were not refreshed. Check the screen's inputs.
- For the same article, Rio Times' own history (29 cases since 2007) shows Vale higher 20 sessions after similar drops in 52% of cases. The worst case fell a further 43%. That is a coin flip, not an edge.
- Peers fell hard on Nov 17: BHP about -5%, Fortescue -5.6%, Rio -2.1% on the ASX. Your screen shows BHP -4.6% and Rio -4.3% today, so the sector rout is continuing.

**What could turn it, and what could extend it**
- **Support:**
  - Chinese analysts put an iron ore floor near $80/t. They say high-cost mines would start cutting output there.
  - UBS puts about 170 Mt of output as loss-making below $90.
  - Goldman puts it at about $95.
  - Hedging, copper and nickel growth, and the low-cost Pilbara producers' margins cushion the earnings hit.
- **Scheduled events.**
  - Miner executives and Australia's prime minister are due to meet Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday (Nov 20). BHP and Rio have supply deals with CMRG, China's state iron ore buyer. Fortescue is still negotiating.
  - Vale Day, with 2027 guidance, is reportedly Dec 1 (one source only, so confirm it).
  - The Fed meets in December. A hike is largely priced, so a hawkish surprise is the risk.
  - The next dividend ex-date is probably in December. Yield estimates ranged from 2% to 7%, so don't use them.
- **Legal:** The UK Mariana (Fundão dam) damages trial is expected around April 2027, so it is unlikely to matter within 1–10 sessions. Vale is reportedly liable for 50% of any award.
- **Vale Base Metals IPO:** Reports were shelved in September. One AKM item dated Nov 5 says it is planned for end-2026, which contradicts them. Treat it as unreliable.

**For the 1–10 session decision**
- A drop of 3.4 average daily ranges with RSI 24 and no turn is a sector-wide commodity slide, not an idiosyncratic one. Whether it bounces depends on iron ore holding $85–88 and on yields, not on Vale news.
- A near-term bounce is plausible if ore holds near the $80s and Friday's Beijing meeting reads constructively. The downside case is ore breaking toward $80 or a hawkish Fed.
- Today's catalyst is unconfirmed. I found no report for the Nov 18 session itself.

**Gaps**
- Bloomberg, Mining.com and Edge Singapore returned 403 errors, so I only have their search snippets. The Nov 18 "floor near $80" article is one of them.
- Rio Times' price feed is unsourced, so I ignored its "iron ore 161.91" figure.

agents.report:
**Discount stores (DG, DLTR, TGT) as of 12:40 PM CT on 2026-11-18**

**Why the basket is up.** Target's Q3 report this morning explains almost all of it. The move in the other two names is a smaller sympathy and re-rating move, and I found no company news from DG or DLTR today.

**Target (TGT), the catalyst**
- Q3 (quarter ended Oct 31): EPS was $2.65 against about $2.07 expected. About $0.50 of that is a one-time IEEPA tariff refund ($301M pretax). Excluding the refund, adjusted EPS rose about 21%.
- Sales and traffic: revenue was $27.07B against $26.56B expected, and net sales rose 7.1%. Comparable sales rose 5.6% against 3.8% expected, with traffic up 5%. CNBC called it Target's best sales growth in five years.
- Mix: digital comparable sales rose nearly 10%. Beauty rose 9% and food and beverage nearly 7%. Sales grew in all three months.
- Guidance: full-year sales growth about 6% (up 1 point). EPS $10.65–$11.40, up from $9.90–$10.90. The operating margin of about 6.2% includes roughly 1.1 points from tariff refunds, so the underlying margin is lower. Management says November is accelerating from October.
- Spending: capex is about $3.8B this year and $5–6B planned next year. Target has also cut prices on thousands of items.
- Stock: reports put TGT at +5% to +7%. It is up more than 70% this year, and it ran into earnings near a $169 level that technical writers flagged. Options had priced a move of about 9%, so +6.7% is inside that. Pre-earnings consensus target was about $169.5, and Telsey's Buy target was $182. I found no post-earnings target changes yet. Those would be useful to check.
- Questions I could not settle: how much of the raised EPS guide is refund rather than operations, and how much of the stock's 70% run is already priced in.

**Dollar Tree (DLTR), next catalyst on Nov 24**
- Dollar Tree reports before the open on Nov 24, which is two sessions after the next one, inside the 1–10 session window. Options implied about a 7.9% move.
- Guidance for Q3 EPS is $0.80–$0.95. Management said the lower year-over-year figure reflects about $0.50 of tariff-refund money reinvested in prices and a $1 price-point promotion for its 40th anniversary. One source puts consensus at $1.39, and another at $0.88. Those conflict, so check the real consensus before relying on either.
- Recent analyst moves: UBS raised its target to $165 (Buy). Stifel initiated at Buy with a $160 target, with shares near $138.70. Loop Capital downgraded to Hold on Nov 5 with a $140 target.
- Dollar Tree received roughly $369–383M in IEEPA refunds in its fiscal Q2. A proposed class action alleges it raised prices on tariffs and then kept the refunds. No court has ruled on that yet.
- Family Dollar was sold in July, so it is no longer in the numbers.

**Dollar General (DG), the laggard at +0.7%**
- On Oct 26 the FTC and 20 states sued over overcharging at checkout (shelf versus register prices). The complaint cites "millions of dollars" in overcharges and "tens of thousands" of complaints. DG said it will defend vigorously and had sent a monetary counteroffer after the FTC's September draft complaint and settlement offer. The stock fell about 4% on the suit. One search summary cited a $1.87B New York settlement. CNBC's article on the suit does not mention New York, and the figure looks implausible, so I treat it as unverified.
- Stifel initiated at Hold with a $145 target. DG opened at $133.52 on Tuesday.
- Q2 (Aug 27): EPS $2.48 (+33%), same-store sales +3.5% (traffic +2.0%), and guidance raised to EPS $7.80–$8.00, including about $0.25 of tariff refund. It also announced up to $700M of buybacks in the second half.
- Next report is likely Dec 3. That date is unconfirmed, and it falls outside a 1–10 session window only if the window is short.

**Macro and sector context**
- Walmart reports before the open on Thursday Nov 19, consensus EPS about $0.64. Last quarter it beat and still fell about 9%. This is the biggest near-term event for the whole group, and it could reverse or extend today's move.
- The theme across all three is tariff refunds (IEEPA tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court on Feb 20, 2026). They flatter EPS now, and the retailers are reinvesting part of them in lower prices. Today's strength rests partly on that.
- Retail also rallied on Nov 4 after the US election, on hopes for lower gas prices and less policy uncertainty.

**Read for the one-to-ten-session decision**
- The basket's move is a single-stock earnings pop in TGT plus partial spillover. A 2.3-standard-deviation stretch against XLP is mostly one name's gap, not a broad rotation into discount retail.
- DG is weighed down by the FTC suit, and DLTR faces an earnings event on Nov 24. Both are poor choices for a pure-momentum follow.
- The main risks are Walmart tomorrow, a fade in TGT after the pop, and the quality of Target's beat (refund-aided).
- Gaps I could not fill: today's intraday closes, post-earnings analyst target changes for TGT, and a reliable DLTR consensus.

Confidence is moderate. The search tool returned many undated or conflicting pages. I found no source that explains today's +2.1% move directly, so the cause below is inferred.

**What most likely drove today (inferred, not confirmed)**
- Managed care is selling off. Alphastreet dated 11/18 has UNH -6.1%, HUM -6.4%, ELV -4.4%, CNC -5.5% and MOH -5.9% in a sector-wide move. Your screen shows UNH about -9% and HUM about -11% at 12:15 PM CT, so the selling has deepened since that report.
- The trigger looks like the CMS "CRUSH" anti-fraud proposal from 11/16. It would let regulators extrapolate Medicare Advantage audit findings across whole contracts, back to payment year 2018. CMS projects about $90B in savings over 2027-2036. UNH fell about 4.6% and CVS about 3% on 11/17 ([Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/unitedhealth-stocks-fall-4-62-183758976.html), [TradingView](https://www.tradingview.com/news/gurufocus:8e8a46678094b:0-cvs-health-stocks-fall-3-12-as-aetna-faces-tougher-medicare-advantage-audit-rules/), [JR Report](https://jrreport.wordandbrown.com/2026/11/17/cms-targets-90b-in-savings-with-sweeping-new-anti-fraud-rule/)).
- Insurers are being crushed and that drags XLV down. A cleaner read of the +2.1% is that devices are holding up while XLV falls, plus some rotation into devices. I could not confirm a rotation, and I found no device-specific news dated today.
- An Investing.com headline, "Medical costs are crushing insurers and lifting LivaNova", suggests a link between insurer weakness and device stocks. I could not open it or date it ([link](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/medical-costs-are-crushing-insurersand-lifting-livanova-stock-5032950)). Higher utilization is bad for insurers and good for procedure volumes.
- The CRUSH rule also limits supply-company outreach to beneficiaries. That could touch durable medical equipment and diabetes supply sellers, but I found no read-through for these fifteen names.

**Sector backdrop (October, so context only)**
- Medtech has had a poor 2026. The S&P 500 health care equipment and supplies index was down more than 20% year to date as of 10/10, against the S&P 500 up about 13%. The causes were Medicaid and ACA policy uncertainty, cyberattacks (BSX and SYK), a BAX recall, thin product launches, and rotation into AI. Tariffs were said to have limited effect ([BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/c9c85aea-9c6e-4865-8cfc-01f0238773b2)).
- Analysts see 2026 as the trough and 2027 as the recovery. Q3 earnings were expected up 4.8%, with Q1 2027 up 13%.
- Barclays initiated 26 medtech names on 10/6 and called the sell-off an overreaction. It said valuations are the lowest in a decade and the discount to the S&P is the widest since the tech bubble ([VCBeat](https://www.vcbeathealth.com/article/63608)). Its ratings and targets:

| Rating | Names (price target) |
|---|---|
| Overweight | SYK ($375), EW ($110), ABT ($120), GEHC ($85), ISRG ($485), DXCM ($115) |
| Neutral | MDT ($95), BSX ($48), ZBH ($100) |
| Underweight | BAX ($20), BDX ($165) |

- The Section 232 medical device tariff probe, opened 9/2/2025, is reportedly still open with no confirmed action. Sources conflict on this, so check the Federal Register. ISRG already builds a roughly 90 basis point tariff hit into its margin guide ([SPS Commerce](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/section-232-medical-device-tariffs-the-investigation-that-never-closed)).

**Name notes**
- **ISRG:** Q3 was reported in late October.
  - Worldwide procedures grew about 15%, da Vinci about 14% and Ion about 31%. US da Vinci growth slowed to 10%.
  - The stock fell about 10% on the report.
  - The 2026 da Vinci procedure guide is 14-15%. Pricing actions will cut instrument revenue per procedure 3-5%.
  - BofA raised its target to $500 on 11/17 and BTIG to $513 on 11/18, per ad-hoc-news (low reliability). The last close I saw was about $430.
- **ABT:** Q3 reported 10/21. Adjusted EPS was $1.42. Diabetes Care grew 6.2%, slower than Q2's 10.4%. Guidance was narrowed to $5.50-5.55 EPS and comparable sales growth cut to about 6%.
  - Exact Sciences closed 3/23/26. A spin of the roughly $8.5B nutrition unit is planned by late 2027. I could not find the stock reaction.
- **BSX:** Down about 52-56% over the past year or since January, near $44-46 in early November, with a 52-week closing low of $41.58 on 10/7.
  - Reasons are WATCHMAN headwinds, the cyberattack, and a soft 2026 guide. The stock jumped 5.6% on 11/2 and fell about 4% on 11/6.
  - Consensus is Buy with a target near $58. A $5B buyback started in May.
- **SYK:** Rose $8.09 to $318.81 on Tuesday 11/17 per MarketBeat. Barclays target is $375, and Citi was reported at $420 (undated).
- **MDT:**
  - Reports fiscal Q2 on Tuesday 11/24 at 5:45 AM CT ([Medtronic](https://news.medtronic.com/2026-11-04-Medtronic-to-announce-financial-results-for-its-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027)). That is about 4 sessions away and inside your 1-10 session window.

**IBN (ICICI Bank ADR): research summary, as of 12:40 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**Caveats on the evidence**
- I found no company-specific catalyst for the move since late October.
- I couldn't find coverage of today's (Nov 18) session. Several results were stale pages with misleading dates, which I excluded.
- A few figures looked inconsistent, and MarketsMojo is partly promotional. I note below where this matters.

**The story: India bank rally with a macro tailwind**
- **Price path (ADR):** The April 2026 low was about $24.99.
  - Nov 4: up 3.8% to about $31.26.
  - Nov 5: new 52-week high of $32.52. 247wallst gave no catalyst, only "sustained buying."
  - Nov 6: about $33.89 (+8.9% from the April low, per 247wallst's later listing).
  - Nov 13: $34.51.
  - Today: 34.82.
  - The screen's 17.9% gain over 20 sessions fits this path. The ADR has been flat to slightly up over the past 5 sessions (+0.2%), so the move is a burst that has stalled, not one still accelerating.
- **Indian listing:** It hit an all-time high of Rs 1,616.7 on Nov 11.
  - It was up 12.8% over one week and 18.6% over one month.
  - It was around Rs 1,583–1,600 on Nov 17. That is slightly below the Nov 11 high, so the local stock is consolidating.
  - It sat near Rs 1,382–1,397 right after Q2 results on Oct 19. That is about a 15% gain in four weeks.
- **Sector backdrop** (Business Today, Nov 16):
  - Bank Nifty was about 52 points under its Feb 3 record of 61,764.85. It had risen 10.4% over the month and 3.2% over the week.
  - Foreign institutions put Rs 66,302 crore into Indian equities in November.
  - Brent fell about 12% from $118 at end-October to roughly $95 on hopes of US-Iran peace talks.
  - Analyst Ponmudi R (Enrich Money) expects short-term consolidation, flags stretched momentum, and says to be selective rather than chase. Resistance for Bank Nifty is 61,300–62,000, and support is 60,700–60,800.
- **Peer comparison:** I couldn't verify the HDB ADR move you cite. One undated page showed HDB near $23.77, but it is too uncertain to use. India bank ADRs rallying together points to a sector or flow-driven move, not an ICICI-specific one.

**Fundamentals (Q2 FY27, reported Oct 17)**
- **Profit and income:**
  - Net profit was Rs 14,843 crore, up 20.1% year on year, and beat expectations.
  - Net interest income was Rs 25,339 crore, up 17.7%.
  - Fee income was up 20.1%.
- **Margin:** Net interest margin fell to 4.18% from 4.36% in Q1 and 4.30% a year earlier. The cause was lower-margin overseas lending and a shift to term deposits. This is the main fundamental weak spot.
- **Asset quality:**
  - Gross NPA ratio is 1.20% (1.38% in June).
  - Net NPA ratio is 0.30%.
  - Provisioning coverage is 75%.
  - It still holds Rs 13,100 crore of contingency provisions.
- **Growth and capital:** Loans grew 30% year on year (24.1% excluding FCNR(B)-linked lending), and deposits grew 27.1%. CET-1 capital is 16.0%.
- **Stock reaction:** The stock fell 1.06% on results day despite the beat, probably on the margin decline.
- **Brokers (Oct 19):**
  - Macquarie: Outperform, target Rs 1,730.
  - Jefferies: Buy, target Rs 1,750.
  - Goldman Sachs: Buy, target Rs 2,025.
  - Jefferies expects FCNR(B) reallocation and loan repricing to support margins.
  - The stock at about Rs 1,600 is now within roughly 8% of the Macquarie and Jefferies targets, so some of the upside is used up. Other sources (Tradingkey, Nov 6) cite an average ADR target of $37.75, which is about 8% above the current price.
- **Valuation (MarketsMojo):** About 19x earnings and 3.18x book value, which it calls a premium to history. It also flags a bearish weekly RSI signal and that non-operating income was 41% of pre-tax profit. Treat it cautiously because it is promotional and had internal inconsistencies.

**Macro risks**
- **RBI:** The Oct 8 report says the RBI raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.5% and shifted to "calibrated tightening." ICICI Bank's economists expect a peak of 6% over the next two meetings. This conflicts with an August item saying the rate was unchanged at 5.25%, which fits a hike having happened in between. I did not find the next meeting date. Rate hikes can help bank margins but hurt bond holdings and credit demand.
- **Oil and flows:** The rally rests on lower crude (a peace-talk hope) and heavy foreign buying. Both can reverse fast, and a setback would hit Indian banks and the ADR.
- **Options positioning:** Headlines mention heavy put and call open interest around the Rs 1,600 strike ahead of the Nov 23 expiry. That makes Rs 1,600 on the Indian listing a likely sticking point.

**Takeaway for the 1–10 session decision**
- The setup is a sector- and flow-driven momentum burst on solid fundamentals, not a news event.
- Technicals are stretched (RSI 78, 4.1 ADRs above the 20-day average), and the sector analyst expects consolidation.
- The Indian stock peaked Nov 11 and has chopped since.
- The ADR is still at highs and has stalled over 5 sessions.
- No scheduled company catalyst turned up inside the window. The main swing factors are oil and US-Iran headlines, foreign flows, and Bank Nifty breaking or failing at the 61,765 record.
- On this evidence, the risk of a pullback or a pause looks larger than the case for chasing here.
- A pullback toward the $31–32 area, where the Nov 4–5 breakout happened, would be a better entry than today's price.

agents.report:
**NOW (ServiceNow): research summary, as of about 12:30 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

I found no ServiceNow-specific news for today. The drop looks like a continuation of last night's software selloff. Several of the sources are low quality or auto-generated recaps, and a few conflict. I note where that matters.

**What happened**
- **Oct 28, after the close: Q3 results.** Subscription revenue was $3.988B, up 21% (20.5% in constant currency). Total revenue was $4.106B against a roughly $4.09B estimate.
  - Adjusted EPS was $1.00 against about $1.02 expected.
  - Q4 cRPO (current remaining performance obligations, the contracted backlog due to be recognized within 12 months) growth was guided to 18.5% in constant currency. Q3 was 21%, and consensus wanted about 19.8%.
  - Full-year subscription guidance rose only $15M at the midpoint, to $15.785B. The free cash flow margin target went to 36% from 35%. The AI annual contract value target went to at least $1.7B from $1.5B.
- **Oct 29: a record one-day drop.** The stock fell about 27%. Evercore's Kirk Materne said the bar was "clearly higher" because the stock had gained about 68% in the prior six months. The Oct 30 session was down a further 4%, to about $105.
- **Management's explanation for the cRPO guide.** Early Q3 renewals pulled in about half of the Q3 cRPO beat. On-premises public-sector deals add roughly a 25 bp headwind, and commerce-related provisions exclude about 50 bp of backlog growth from cRPO. The CFO conceded cRPO is "certainly not perfect" as an indicator. Deployment support for large AI deals cut reported growth by about 25 bp in Q3 and is expected to cut about 50 bp in Q4.
- **Other negatives cited (Zacks, Nov 11).**
  - Subscription gross margin fell to about 74% from 80% a year earlier.
  - Debt rose to about $7.5B from $1.5B at the end of 2025, after the Armis deal (about $7.75B, closed in April).
  - Armis is expected to cut non-GAAP operating margin by about 75 bp.
  - 2026 EPS estimates were cut 2.7% over 30 days.
- **Nov 16 and 17: the slide continued.**
  - Nov 16: down 2.9% to about $99, on volume about half the average.
  - Nov 17: down 6.5% to a $92.90 close, with no company news. The cited causes are AI-disruption fears for per-seat software and the pending Anthropic IPO. A Trefis piece says it is expected to list on Nasdaq as ANT on Nov 19.
  - Nov 17 context: Salesforce fell about 9.5%, IGV (the software ETF) about 3.3%, and 25 of 28 systems-software peers fell. The S&P 500 hit a five-month low.
  - Tickeron cites a 10-year yield above 5%, December rate-hike expectations and new AI-chip export limits as macro pressure. I treat that as a weak single source.
- **Today.** A Tickeron widget showed $90.94 at 12:09 PM Eastern (about 11:09 AM CT), down 2.1%. That is consistent with your 89.54.

**Price and technicals**
- The 52-week closing high was $173.50 on Dec 11, 2025. Sources give an April 2026 low of $81.24, which is the nearest reference level below the current price. They quote a $175 intraday high.
- The stock is far below its 50-day average (about $132) and its 200-day average (about $114).
- RSI and stochastics have been oversold for about 12 to 13 days, per Tickeron. Its own commentary says the bearish crossover signals have often been followed by gains, which is mixed evidence.
- Tickeron also reports put activity above normal.

**Analysts and flows**
- MarketBeat shows consensus "Moderate Buy" with an average target of about $154.50 (1 Strong Buy, 36 Buy, 3 Hold, 3 Sell). TipRanks shows about $163.50. These averages are stale because many firms are still cutting targets.
- Citi cut its target to $157 from $170 and kept Buy. KeyBanc is Underweight with a $110 target (raised from $85), which is now above the share price.
- Cantor raised its target to $201 and RBC is at $165 (Outperform). Bernstein reiterated Outperform with a $266 target, and JPMorgan is at $160.
- **Insiders.** A Form 4 shows Jacqueline Canney sold 2,475 shares on Nov 16 under a 10b5-1 plan. Other recent insider activity is also small sales. CEO Bill McDermott bought about $3M in February.
- **Buyback.** About $4.2B of buyback authorization remained at Sep 30. I found no disclosure of Q4 repurchases and no activist stake.

**Valuation**
- About 26x the $3.95 consensus 2026 EPS and about 21x 2027 (an author's estimate), or about 5.5x forward sales (Zacks). Another source puts it at 6.2x trailing sales.

**Bull and bear cases**
- **Bull:**
  - Growth is still about 21%, renewals are at 98%, and free cash flow guidance went up.
  - AI is growing: net new AI ACV is up 65% and deals above $1M are up 4.5 times.
  - Management says about half of net new business is already non-seat-priced (a Zacks-derived claim of unclear date).
  - The stock is down about 45% year over year and about 46% from its high, with a deeply oversold reading.
- **Bear:**
  - The cRPO deceleration and the AI-versus-seats narrative are unresolved.
  - Margin and debt pressure from Armis.
  - Estimates are still being cut, and the Oct 28 low-quality beat means the next real data is not until late January.
  - The Anthropic IPO and the sector's heavy selling pressure could continue.

**Near-term catalysts**
- **Today:** the Nvidia reaction.
- **Nov 19:** Intuit earnings and the Anthropic IPO.
- **Nov 24:** Workday earnings.
- **Dec 2:** Salesforce earnings.
- **Late January:** NOW Q4 results.
- **Not found:** no NOW-specific catalyst inside the 1 to 10 session window.

**Read for a 1 to 10 session decision**
The decline is a sector-driven, narrative-driven capitulation on top of a post-earnings gap, not a company-specific break. Within the window, the stock will most likely follow the software group. That makes a snap-back from this oversold level plausible, but the evidence for a turn is thin. The selling pressure has persisted for three weeks on slight volume spikes, and the Nov 19 Anthropic and Intuit events are risks in both directions. A cleaner entry signal would be software stabilizing, for example IGV holding after Intuit and the ANT debut. The $81 April low is the next reference level below.
